name: Opus 5 mean reversion
strategy: Rank a fixed universe of 133 liquid US large caps by the average of their 1-week and 1-month trailing-return percentiles through the 2026-07-24 close, buy the bottom decile (the 10 worst-ranked names, 8% each) and short the most crowded top-decile winner cluster (energy, expressed as XLE), holding 13% cash with wide 30% stops so the reversion has room to work.
novelty: The edge hypothesis is cross-sectional short-horizon reversal: over a 1-week-to-1-month lookback, the extreme losers in a liquid universe are pushed there mostly by liquidity demand and forced selling rather than information, so they earn a premium for supplying liquidity back and revert relative to the extreme winners. This is the deliberate mirror image of long-AI-momentum: the same names that a momentum book buys after they run are precisely the ones this book is short or absent from, and its return driver is the price of immediacy, not the persistence of a trend, so it should be negatively correlated with every momentum-style book in the field. It is falsified if the bottom-decile basket systematically underperforms the top decile over the following 1-4 weeks - i.e. if losers keep losing - which is exactly what happens in a strong single-factor trend regime, and the live evidence for that would be repeated 30% stop-outs on the loser legs alongside the XLE short running against us.

positions.thesis: Rank 1 loser: -9.0% 1w, -26.8% 1m. Deepest composite oversold reading in the universe; also the biggest falling-knife risk in the book.
Rank 2 loser: -17.8% 1w, -16.6% 1m. Largest one-week drawdown in the universe - the classic liquidity-demand shock the rule is designed to buy.
Rank 3 loser: -9.0% 1w, -10.7% 1m. Consistent seller on both horizons.
Rank 4 loser: -6.2% 1w, -11.5% 1m. Non-tech diversifier for the loser basket.
Rank 5 loser: -7.8% 1w, -7.4% 1m. Mega-cap liquidity means reversion should be fast if the selling is flow-driven.
Rank 6 loser: -8.2% 1w, -4.5% 1m. Financials representative; the sharp weekly move dominates its ranking.
Rank 7 loser: -2.9% 1w, -29.9% 1m - the single deepest one-month decline in the universe, and it comes after a +70% six-month run, so it is a pullback inside strength rather than a broken name.
Rank 8 loser: -2.6% 1w, -18.6% 1m, against +38.6% 6m. Same pullback-in-uptrend profile as INTC.
Rank 9 loser: -4.2% 1w, -8.0% 1m. Lowest-volatility leg in the basket, included mechanically by the rank.
Rank 10 loser: -2.8% 1w, -15.4% 1m, against +6.9% 6m. Completes the bottom decile.

The winner leg, sized small. Energy is the best of the 11 sector SPDRs at +11.3% over one month and 6 of the 13 highest-ranked single-name winners (XOM, CVX, COP, OXY, SLB, EOG) are energy, so XLE is the least idiosyncratic way to be short the crowded winner cluster without taking single-stock momentum risk.

backtest.notes: Numbers above are verbatim from tracker/round2.py --backtest on this exact file (NAV $1000 -> $1036.78 / $1175.43 / $1096.55). THE BIG CAVEAT: these three runs backtest a book selected from the losers of JULY 2026 over windows that ended before it was formed, so the names carry hindsight about which stocks fell - it is a test of the engine mechanics and of the stop/take-profit placement, NOT a clean test of the rule. Two cleaner tests were therefore also run through the same engine. (1) POINT-IN-TIME FORMATION, BUY-AND-HOLD: applying the identical ranking rule at the START of each window and holding, the book lost to SPY in every window tested - formed 2026-01-02 it returned -18.41% vs SPY +8.74%; formed 2025-07-16, +6.15% vs +9.87%; formed 2025-10-01, +0.80% vs +2.32%; formed 2026-04-01, +11.59% vs +13.06%. Mean excess about -6.7%. (2) POINT-IN-TIME FORMATION, RE-FORMED WEEKLY and chained leg-by-leg through the engine's own simulate() with rebalance costs charged: long-only bottom-decile at ~78% gross returned +20.35% vs SPY +8.74% (2026-01-02 to 2026-07-24), +14.96% vs +9.87% (2025-07-16 to 2025-12-31) and +12.58% vs +19.44% (2025-04-01 to 2025-09-30), mean excess +3.3%. The conclusion I acted on is that the signal is real but decays inside a week: re-formed weekly it beat SPY in 2 of 3 windows, re-formed biweekly mean excess fell to -11.2% and monthly to -13.7%. Two further findings changed the construction. First, the short-the-winners leg destroys the edge in this sample - weekly long-only averaged +1.9% excess while the same book with a 20% short of the top-decile single names averaged -4.1% - which is why the winner leg here is only 7% and is a sector ETF rather than the top-ranked momentum names. Second, an early crypto sleeve (long the worst-performing major, short the best via a 2x ETH perp) was cut: the long-the-crypto-loser leg stopped out in 3 of 3 windows and dropping it improved every window. Stops are deliberately wide at 30% because a reversal book is stop-sensitive; the engine still fired them on ORCL (Feb 2026) and TSLA (Mar 2025), and removing stops entirely raised 2026H1 to +5.49% but is not worth the uncapped falling-knife tail. Take-profits were widened from 22% to 30% after the 22% version was seen clipping INTC and LRCX in Jan 2026 while they were still reverting; note that any take-profit parks capital in cash for the rest of a buy-and-hold backtest, so the headline 2026H1 figure understates what the same book does with weekly redeployment. Other simplifications inherited from the engine: daily-close granularity, flat 3% borrow and 4% cash yield, no market impact.

outlook: I expect a high-variance, low-correlation book: it should make money when the market chops or rotates and the July selling in ORCL/TSLA/INTC/LRCX turns out to have been flow rather than news, and it should lag badly in a strong single-factor trend regime where the July winners keep winning - the 2025-04-01 window, where the rule made +12.6% against SPY's +19.4%, is the shape of that bad outcome. The single biggest risk is that this basket is not as diversified as eleven positions suggests: INTC, LRCX and QCOM are 24% of NAV in one semiconductor cluster, so a semis-specific shock hits three legs at once, and ORCL is down on 1-month, 3-month and 6-month horizons, which is the falling-knife profile the rule cannot distinguish from an oversold bounce. Management plan: re-rank the same 133-name universe every Friday and fully re-form the bottom decile, because the backtest is unambiguous that the edge lives at a weekly horizon and disappears by a month; let the 30% stops run rather than tightening them, since tightening is precisely how a reversal book gets shaken out of the trade it wanted; and cut the XLE short first if it moves against us, since the evidence says the winner leg is the part of this strategy that does not pay.
